messages:
Evan (AE): quick sync — SupplyChainX asking for enterprise commit. They want predictable cost + p95 < 350ms. Traffic profile: steady ~800 rps with 10–15m spikes up to 3k rps during day. Also ~50 qps embeddings. Need a capacity proposal + pricing sketch ASAP.

Maya (Solutions Eng): clarifying q: are the 800 rps steady chat requests (short tokens) or long gen jobs? and any regional constraints?

Evan (AE): mixed. ~70% chat (median ~30 tokens), ~30% long generation (~400 tokens). Primary region us-west-2, secondary us-east-1 for DR. They require AZ failover and VPC/private deployment for PII.

Ravi (Runtime): high-level calc to start: tokens/sec = rps * avg_tokens. steady tokens: 800 * 30 = 24k tps. spike tokens: 3k * 400 = 1.2M tps (but spikes are mostly long gens? they said mixed; assume worst-case overlap). GPUs capacity varies by model/quant. For our quantized Llama variant, conservative throughput ~150k tokens/sec per A100-ish equivalent under small-batch gen. So baseline: 24k tps ==> 1 GPU headroom. But to meet p95 <350ms and concurrency, we need multiple replicas to absorb seq-latency and batching overhead.

Maya (Solutions Eng): pragmatic proposal: reserved pool sized for steady + buffer for canary/autoscale warmups, plus a small burst pool for short spikes.

Priya (Infra): propose config: min_replicas=3 (reserved), warm_pool=2, burst_pool=2, max_replicas=9 across AZs. That gives fast autoscale for chat and room to spin up extra gen workers. We'll pin primary to us-west-2 and allow cross-AZ failover.

Ravi (Runtime): sample autoscale policy (pseudo-config):
```
policy: throughput
min_replicas: 3
warm_pool: 2  # prewarmed instances kept ready
burst_pool: 2 # short-lived burst capacity (paid as burst credits)
max_replicas: 9
scale_up_threshold: 70% token_utilization
scale_down_cooldown: 120s
region_affinity: [us-west-2, us-east-1]
```
This is a starting point. Warm_pool reduces p95 during spikes.

Evan (AE): Jorge, how do we price reserved + burst? Customer expects a commit discount but also wants to handle bursts.

Jorge (Finance): suggest reserved pricing for baseline (3 reserved GPUs) with monthly commit, add priced burst credits for 2 burst GPUs and pay-as-you-go for extra autoscale beyond max_replicas. Example: reserved discount 25% off hourly; burst credits priced at on-demand with 30% uplift. We'll run numbers once we pick GPU type and expected hours.

Maya (Solutions Eng): also flag: mixed workload means KV cache pressure for long gens. Recommend enabling prefix caching for the chat portion to cut token cost ~15–25%. We'll include quantization recommendation for long gens (8-bit) to increase GPU density.

Priya (Infra): security notes from private deployment checklist: KMS-managed keys, VPC peering, SOC2 docs. They also asked for data residency proof for EU customers — we can provide region isolation.

Evan (AE): POC ask: they want a 72-hour ramp with production-like traces. Can we simulate their mixed profile and capture p95, tail, and token-cost numbers?

Ravi (Runtime): SGTM. Need sample trace or at least QPS/time series + token-length histogram. If we don't get trace, we'll generate synthetic based on the ratios (70/30 chat/gen) and run three-phase ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% steady, then inject two 10–15m 3k spikes. We'll attach a short runbook for how we're running it.

Maya (Solutions Eng): I'll follow up on the eval prompt set and provide a QC checklist (latency SLOs, correctness smoke tests). Also we should add an eval for quality regression when using quantized weights.

Evan (AE): action items: @Maya prep eval and runbook; @Ravi estimate GPU type + perf numbers; @Priya prepare private deployment checklist and preheat steps; @Jorge draft pricing sketch. Customer target decision date: 2 weeks.

Ravi (Runtime): initial rough numbers I'll drop tomorrow, but my early recommendation: reserved 4 GPUs (balanced for steady + buffer), warm_pool 2, burst 2, allow autoscale to 9 for rare sustained peaks. We'll tune after POC.

Jorge (Finance): I'll produce two pricing scenarios: (A) conservative reserve (3 GPUs + burst) and (B) aggressive reserve (5 GPUs, lower burst). Deliver by EOD Thursday.

deploy-bot: scheduled test cluster for SupplyChainX POC at 2025-11-03T14:00:00Z.

Maya (Solutions Eng): SGTM. Also add note: need completed security questionnaire for Private offering before we start POC. I'll send the doc to their security team.

Evan (AE): perfect — thanks all. I'll book a 30m sync after Jorge's pricing. :thumbsup:

Priya (Infra): one more perf tip — run the long-gen jobs on separate instance pools to avoid queueing chat requests; use routing policy by workload-type.

Ravi (Runtime): agreed — route by route tag. We'll add a fallback policy to a lighter quantized model if we hit sustained capacity errors.

Evan (AE): noted. Closing for now, will reopen if customer provides traces/questions.
